findings.title: Inline shutdown fallback runs adapter release() on the request worker: extra self-wait, self-interrupt, swallowed Error
findings.description: When t.start() throws, runShutdownSequence runs on the request thread. adapter.stop(left) then waits for (and on timeout aborts) the very exchange that called shutdown, and a.release() waits the adapter's fixed release margin for its own worker pool, which contains the current thread; InMemoryHttpAdapter.release() then calls shutdownNow(), interrupting the calling request thread, which goes back into the handler (res.send) with the interrupt flag set. So the call takes timeout + release margin, not 'up to the timeout' as docs/api/lifecycle.md says, and that request's response is force-closed. The caught Throwable is also dropped without a log line, so the operator never learns the shutdown thread could not be created. OOM path only, hence LOW.
findings.suggested_fix: Log the caught Throwable at ERROR (best effort) before running inline, and say in lifecycle.md that in this fallback the calling request's response is force-closed at the timeout and the call may also take the adapter's release margin; optionally clear the interrupt flag the self-release leaves on the request thread.

findings.title: New public API RotatingFileLogger.rotationFailureCount() and the rotation back-off/backup-preserving behavior are not in FR-APP-017 or the wave-4 SDS
findings.description: The fix adds a public method and two observable behaviors (rotation retried only after another maxFileBytes; oldest backup deleted only when every slot is taken). docs/api/logging.md documents them, but FR-APP-017 (requirement text and AC-2) and SDS wave-4-9 Interfaces list only droppedCount(); CLAUDE.md forbids behavior not covered by an SRS requirement. The new test cites FR-APP-017 AC-2, whose text does not mention these behaviors.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an FR-APP-017 AC (via speckiwi MCP) covering rotationFailureCount() and the failed-rename back-off, or fold it into AC-2's Decision line.
